blocks.text: A route proves that two places can make contact, not that they share an economy. Durable connection means production on one continent responds to demand on another, while distant changes affect local exchange and life.

Silver connected Andean mines, Chinese markets and transoceanic commerce. Production, transport, monetary demand and political organization were located separately yet interacted through repeated movement. People who never met could participate in the same economic circuit.

blocks.caption: Spanish Atlantic Empire · Context illustration; historical interpretation is in the text.

blocks.text: This was not simply one active center surrounded by passive places. Markets and resource positions jointly influenced flows, while maritime empires, merchants and communities held unequal power. Wider connections allowed local changes to have distant consequences.

A global system therefore means more than additional routes on a map. Resources, people, risks and causes began to travel repeatedly across continents. Understanding the system still requires regional differences: global connection did not create identical global circumstances.
